newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's NYBB upgrades MOL to "buy".
newsitem.headline: Hungary's NYBB upgrades MOL to "buy".

text.p: Hungarian securities house New York Broker Budapest upgraded oil and gas company MOL Rt to short-term and long-term "buy" from short-term and long-term "hold" on both fundamental and technical grounds.

"The company strengthened its market positions, boosting its wholesale market share to 86 percent (up nine percent) in engine gasoline and to 89 percent (up three percent) in gas and heating oils," analyst Gabriella Bor said in a desknote.
The analyst was referring to MOL's performance in the first quarter of the year over the same period of last year.
MOL reported an IAS consolidated net income of 12.737 billion forints, up from 8.420 billion in the first quarter of 1996.
Bor expected MOL to generate lower results in the next two quarters due to seasonality, but "looking at 12-month figures the accumulated earnings per share shows a rising trend".

On the technical side, Bor said MOL had significant support at 3,065 forints, therefore its price was unlikely to fall below that level. She said MOL's price hovered above the shorter-term moving averages which makes a bullish trend probable.
At 1031 GMT on the Budapest Stock Exchange MOL shares traded at 3,390 forints, down 10.
